title: Erica Campbell’s Label Sues Distributor Over Gospel Music Royalties
summary: SRG/ILS Group was previously hit with a similar lawsuit from R&B singer Kenny Lattimore.
body: Indie record label My Block Inc. is suing distributor SRG/ILS Group over royalty accounting for Erica Campbell ‘s 2023 gospel album I Love You . A Thursday (Sept. 17) lawsuit, first obtained and reported by Billboard , alleges that SRG hasn’t provided a single royalty statement to My Block, the label founded by Erica Campbell’s husband, producer Warryn Campbell . The case comes in the wake of similar legal claims brought by veteran R&B singer Kenny Lattimore against the digital distributor, which operates in partnership with Universal Music Group’s Virgin Music. title: Google could be working on an incognito upgrade for Gemini Live
summary: Because not everything you show to Gemini is something you want it to remember.
body: TL;DR Google appears to be developing an “Ephemeral Video Mode” for Gemini Live. It’s possible that this could essentially let you go incognito for a Live session, while still working with video input. Normally, video shared with Live is archived in your Gemini Apps Activity. Not every interaction we have with AI needs to take place under the same constraints — and well-designed systems will give us the control we need to dial that in, just how we want it. Sometimes, privacy is going to be paramount, and we want the AI forgetting about the whole interaction the second it’s over. Other times, context is everything, and we want the AI remembering everything for future sessions. Right now we’re wondering if Google could be working on an upgrade for Gemini Live along these lines, as we spot reference to a curious new “Ephemeral” mode. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: Google reveals how its new 3D emoji were designed, and which Android brands are getting them
summary: Plus an exhaustive preview, ready to search.
body: TL;DR Google introduced Noto 3D emoji, its latest redesign, back in May around Google I/O. The new set has now started to roll out with devices like the Pixel 11, but availability is still very limited. Google is now sharing a list of manufacturers who will be getting Noto 3D on their phones. Emoji on Android are getting a fresh new look. Back in May, Google first shared its latest emoji overhaul with the presentation of its Noto 3D set. Beyond just picking up a new 3D look, familiar emoji are getting a glow up with a lot more detail. Now they’re finally starting to arrive, but if you’ve still got questions about who’s getting access, or what exactly all these new emoji are going to look like, we’ve spotted some answers. We first saw Noto 3D emoji hitting phones with the release of the Pixel 11 series. And now with more devices moving to Android 17 and related platforms, like Nothing OS 5.0 , they’re finally starting to spread. Now Google Design is sharing a closer look at how Noto 3D came to be — and who’s getting it next.

title: Google’s upcoming custom clocks could be easy to edit and move between Pixels
summary: Your custom designs could follow you.
body: TL;DR Google is still developing its AI-generated lock screen clocks, with the feature not yet functional in Android Canary builds. New strings suggest users will be able to edit, delete, rate, and generate multiple AI clock styles. Google also appears to be working on cloud backup and device-to-device transfer, so your custom clocks could follow you to a new phone. Google has steadily been increasing the amount of control it gives users over lock screen customization. The tech giant finally gave us our lock screen widgets back last year, after taking them away all the way back in 2014 with Android 5. Now, it seems to be taking that customization a step further. title: This tiny, beloved e-reader is getting a successor that runs on Android
summary: Xteink S4 doubles the battery and ditches Linux for Android 11.
body: Credit: Good e-Reader TL;DR A spiritual successor to the Xteink X4 is coming. The Xteink S4 will run on Android 11, allowing you to sideload from reading apps like Kindle, Kobo, and KOReader. It will come with 2GB of RAM, 32GB of storage, and a 1,400mAh battery. When Xteink launched the Xteink X4, it made a big impression on e-reader fans. The pocketable E-Ink device was great for DRM-free reading, and it was small enough to fit on the back of most phones. However, nothing is perfect, and improvements can always be made. Enter the spiritual successor to the Xteink X4. Good e-Reader reports that the Chinese startup behind the Xteink X4 is launching the Xteink S4. The Xteink S4 has a 4.3 E-Ink touchscreen that offers 220 PPI. It’s said to weigh 95 grams and is 6.98mm thick. However, what’s particularly notable is the operating system.

title: Sharing Google Photos albums via QR codes may soon become way easier
summary: An effective alternative to the existing screenshot-based solution in Google Photos.
body: TL;DR Google Photos could soon add Copy and Download buttons to its QR code-based album-sharing interface. In its current form, Google Photos encourages users to capture a screenshot of the code to share with their contacts. We have also uncovered a new bottom sheet that introduces users to the updated Collections tab. Google Photos has let you share albums with a link for some time now. Last year, the app gained a QR code-based solution to make things easier. However, it doesn’t let you directly download the QR code to your phone, with Google recommending users to take a screenshot instead. A future update to the Photos app may finally fix this. title: YouTube’s watch next suggestions are crossing the line on Android — literally
summary: The UI bug is obscuring the YouTube progress bar for many.
body: TL;DR Some YouTube users on Android say suggested videos are covering the full screen player and blocking the progress bar. Reports of the issue date back to at least April, with several new complaints surfacing recently. Google hasn’t publicly acknowledged the problem yet, so it’s unclear whether this is a bug or an intentional UI test. YouTube’s recommendation algorithm is one of its biggest strengths. Regardless of the topic you’re exploring, the platform does a good job of surfacing more relevant content to watch next. Lately, though, those recommendations appear to be getting a little too aggressive for a large subset of users. An increasing number of YouTube users on Android are seeing suggested videos appearing over the bottom portion of the player in full screen, essentially obscuring a part of the video and the progress bar, all while making it impossible to scrub through a video.

title: Some YouTube users are stuck watching videos in low resolution
summary: YouTube is stuck playing videos like it's the old days.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube users are reporting that they can only watch videos in 480p resolution. The problem appears to be affecting both free and Premium users. Some say clearing the app’s cache or uninstalling and reinstalling fixes the issue, but others say those methods did not work for them. YouTube recently fixed an issue that prevented users from signing up, adding packages, or modifying their subscriptions. With that concern taken care of, hopefully, the team will now be able to turn its attention to another problem that has crept up. The problem in question is forcing users to watch videos at lower resolutions. YouTube allows you to watch videos in a variety of resolutions, all the way up to 4K. In most cases, you’ll at least be able to choose from a range between 240p and 1080p. However, the number of available resolution options has been cut short for some users.

title: Another Motorola phone just picked up its big Android 17 update
summary: The 4.3GB update adds new notification tools, widgets, and more.
body: TL;DR Motorola is rolling out the stable Android 17 update to the Edge 70, making it the company’s second phone to get the new OS. The 4.3GB update adds stackable widgets, themed icons, Live Updates, notification summaries, and other improvements. But users are reporting that the depth-effect lock screen wallpaper is missing from the stable release. Motorola’s Android 17 story has been something of a slow burn. What began with beta testing in February was followed by a broader list of eligible phones last month, before the stable update finally debuted on the Motorola Signature . Now the rollout is reaching its second device, with Android 17 beginning to land on the Motorola Edge 70. Multiple Edge 70 owners are reporting that Android 17 has arrived on their phones, and Motorola has also published an official changelog for the update. The download weighs about 4.3GB and carries build number A17WRH.35-10.

title: Roku will soon let you test exciting new features before they go live
summary: Roku is also making search smarter and Voice more useful.
body: TL;DR Roku Labs will soon let US users test experimental features directly from the Home Screen and provide feedback before wider rollouts. Roku is also rolling out smarter search explanations, weather information through Roku Voice, and discounted subscription bundles in the US and Mexico. Roku’s redesigned Home Screen is expanding to Brazil and Mexico, while Roku LT OS is going open source for developers and hardware projects. Roku may be raising hardware prices , but at least users can rest assured that they’re getting some value from their streaming dollar, as the company previews its latest Roku OS update, including enhanced search, its revamped home screen expansion, and most importantly, a new way for users to test experimental features before they’re ready for prime time. The San Jose-based announces the big update in a blog post today, and it’s clear that the streaming giant’s focus is on letting users share feedback and directly influence new features.

title: YouTube plays whack-a-mole, fixes another annoying account issue
summary: The issue affected sign-ups, add-ons, and subscription changes.
body: TL;DR YouTube and YouTube TV briefly had issues with sign-ups and subscription management. Some users saw errors when trying to add packages or change existing subscriptions. Google says the issue is fixed, but users still having trouble should refresh the app or browser. YouTube just closed the book on a sign-in bug that locked some people out of the app on smart TVs and gaming consoles. That issue was fixed earlier this week, but another account-related problem surfaced soon after. This time, the trouble hit people trying to sign up for or change paid subscriptions across YouTube and YouTube TV — and Google says it has already fixed that too. In a community post , YouTube said some users ran into errors or failed dialog boxes when trying to sign up, add packages, or modify existing subscriptions. The company said it was investigating the issue, but didn’t identify the cause or say how many people were affected.

title: I used the Motorola Edge (2026) all summer long, but it never won me over
summary: A pretty face just isn't enough.
body: I’m one of the bigger Motorola fans at Android Authority . If nothing else, I’ve spent the most time with a Moto phone in my pocket, ranging from several generations of the dirt-cheap Moto G to the recent heights of the ultra-premium (and Ultra-branded) Motorola Razr Ultra . There’s just something about the clean Android experience and fun Pantone colors that has always spoken to me; what can I say? In that time, though, I’ve watched Motorola’s Edge series go through the wringer. I remember when it first rolled out as a flagship, only to become an affordable flagship-style option a year or two later, and before finally settling as a sub-$600 mid-ranger. And yet, there was still plenty to like about the Edge, even at its cheaper price point.

title: I use Waze every day, and the latest Android Auto update completely changed how I drive
summary: Gemini knows all my Waze now.
body: Gemini is pretty much everywhere in Google’s world at this point. It’s baked into Pixel phones , across Google’s apps , and has even made its way into Chrome . So whenever I opened Waze, I couldn’t help but wonder why one of Google’s most popular navigation apps was still missing out. I use Waze pretty much every time I’m behind the wheel — it handles navigation well; it warns me about a speed camera coming up, tells me about a hazard on the road, or gives me a heads-up when traffic starts piling up ahead.

title: Galaxy S25 and older models finally have a One UI 9 rollout date
summary: The rollout roadmap also points to October for older Galaxy flagships.
body: TL;DR Samsung has revealed a clearer roadmap for when One UI 9 will expand beyond the Galaxy S26 series. The Galaxy S25 series and Galaxy Z Fold 7/Flip 7 will start receiving One UI 9 on September 28. The Galaxy S23 FE is slated for October, hinting that the Galaxy S24 and S23 series could also follow that month. Samsung’s stable One UI 9 rollout is finally underway , with the Galaxy S26 series first in line for the Android 17-based update. That still left owners of the Galaxy S25 series and older flagships wondering when their turn would come, but Samsung has now quietly provided a much clearer roadmap for the next phase of the rollout. In an official One UI 9 rollout announcement , Samsung Thailand says the Galaxy S25 series, Galaxy Z Fold 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 will start receiving the Android 17-based update on September 28. The same announcement says the Galaxy S23 FE will follow sometime in October.

title: 5 reasons I’ll always pick the Galaxy S26 Ultra over the iPhone 18 Pro Max
summary: The iPhone 18 Pro Max is great, but these five Samsung features win me over.
body: The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra and Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max are about as evenly matched as flagship phones come. Both pack phenomenal cameras, blistering performance, excellent displays, and enough battery life to comfortably get through a busy day. On paper, there’s arguably less separating these two giants than ever. But specifications aren’t everything, and there are still several features that would make me pick Samsung’s Ultra over Apple’s latest Pro Max. Some are big headline features, while others are clever little touches that make a difference in everyday use.

title: One of the most popular smart home hubs is getting a sizeable price increase
summary: US customers will now have to spend 40% more to buy the smart home hub.
body: TL;DR The Philips Hue Bridge Pro has seen a significant price increase in the US, reportedly in mid-August. Meanwhile, customers in Europe are witnessing an even steeper price increase for the smart home hub. Additionally, Europe is seeing higher prices on other Philips Hue products, such as smart light strips. The global components shortage has already hit the tech industry hard. As a result, we’ve already seen price hikes across smartphones, computers, gaming consoles, and several other segments. It now looks like popular smart home products aren’t exempt either, as the Philips Hue Bridge Pro is facing a similar fate. A quick look at the Philips Hue page shows a $139.99 price tag for the Bridge Pro, a $40 increase over the smart home hub’s launch-day price (via Hue Blog ). Similarly, the Amazon listing also reflects the same $139.99 price, suggesting the updated price is live everywhere.

title: Google turned Pixel Themes into a bloatware ad platform, and I hate it
summary: How did it all go so wrong?
body: Last November, Google added something pretty exciting to Pixel phones: a new feature called “Pixel Themes.” Pixels have long trailed other Android phones in home screen and system customization, so the prospect of a new theme system sounded like just what the doctor ordered. As it turns out, that couldn’t have been further from the truth.

title: iPhone 18 Pro battery numbers are both good and bad news for Samsung
summary: Want to hold on to your phone for more than a couple of years? A Samsung phone might be the better bet.
body: TL;DR The EU’s energy database has revealed the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s battery capacities. The database also reveals that these iPhones are still rated for 1,000 charging cycles, lagging behind many Android phones. A third-party charging test reveals that the iPhone 18 Pro Max is also the fastest charging iPhone ever. Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max last week, and it had plenty to say about them. The company doesn’t traditionally share battery capacity, though, but a regulatory source has now revealed these details and more. The European Union’s EPREL database has revealed that the iPhone 18 Pro has a 4,056mAh battery, a negligible upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro’s 3,988mAh battery. On the other hand, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is listed with a 5,391mAh battery, which is a significant upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s 4,823mAh battery.

title: Claude can now automatically choose which mode is best for you
summary: Chat vs. Cowork: Claude is asking you to make one less decision before it gets to work.
body: Credit: Mitja Rutnik / Android Authority TL;DR Anthropic is eliminating a major source of friction in its chat interface. Claude can now automatically choose between Chat and Cowork modes based on the complexity of your task. Along with this, Claude can now output directly into information-dense media using Docs, Slides, or Design. Deciding among all the different AI tools and their respective models can already lead to choice fatigue. If you use Claude, it may add another layer of decision-making by making you choose between Chat and Cowork. Of the two, Chat executes tasks in a simpler chatbot interface, while Cowork offloads them to an autonomous agent that can work in the background. While it’s easy to choose between the two for simpler tasks, the decision may feel overwhelming when you’re working on a more complex task that requires extensive research or analysis. To alleviate this pressure, Anthropic has decided to do away with the toggle in Claude entirely. In a blog post , the frontier lab noted that it was merging Chat and Cowork features, and Claude will be able to choose between the two on its own.

title: Samsung could give the Galaxy S27 Ultra a major camera processing upgrade
summary: Samsung may also improve dynamic range and its professional video tools.
body: TL;DR The Galaxy S27 Ultra could get updated Samsung Log and APV support for improved dynamic range. Samsung is also rumored to be reworking photo color processing for warmer, more natural-looking results. These changes could complement other rumored camera upgrades, including a new 200MP main sensor and refreshed ultrawide and selfie cameras. Samsung’s Galaxy Ultra cameras have evolved in small steps lately, but its video stack has moved more noticeably. The Galaxy S24 Ultra already offered 4K/120fps and 8K/30fps recording, the S25 Ultra added Samsung Log, and the S26 Ultra introduced Samsung’s APV codec . A new Galaxy S27 Ultra leak now suggests Samsung could build on those tools without raising the headline recording resolution. A relatively unknown X user, WalleGalaxy , claims the Galaxy S27 Ultra will support updated versions of Samsung Log and APV (Advanced Professional Video), potentially delivering greater dynamic range than the S26 Ultra. Recording reportedly remains capped at 4K/120fps and 8K/30fps.

title: This new Android skin copies iOS 27 so perfectly, it might even fool Apple
summary: I bet it also has a Liquid Glass adjustment slider somewhere in the settings.
body: TL;DR HONOR has revealed its new Android 17-based skin: Magic OS 11. It copies Apple’s Liquid Glass design on the home screen, navigation bars, quick settings, and everywhere else. It’s expected to debut with the HONOR Magic 9 series later this month. It’s no secret that everyone in the tech industry copies each other. Apple frequently “borrows” features from Android brands and markets them as game-changing innovations, while Android manufacturers often copy Apple’s software and industrial design. However, HONOR has now gone above and beyond, copying the iOS Liquid Glass look so thoroughly that it’s nearly identical. HONOR showed off its Magic OS 11 Android skin at its Global Developer Conference, and it’s hard to say it’s merely “inspired” by iOS. It feels like the company took a screenshot of an iPhone and asked its designers to replicate it with Android elements. To be fair, it will go really well with the HONOR Magic 9 Pro Max’s design .

title: Dell may have spilled the beans on its first XPS Googlebook
summary: Dell might rely on the XPS brand name to position its premium Googlebook.
body: TL;DR Dell’s first Googlebook will be launched under the XPS name, according to a leaked document spotted online. It’s internally codenamed “Mica” and could have the model number DX13267. This corroborates an earlier Geekbench leak that pointed to the same model number. As we head toward the expected October 5 Googlebook launch , we’re steadily getting more leaks and rumors about the first wave of devices. Early last month, a Geekbench listing suggested Dell’s Googlebook might arrive under the company’s famed “XPS” name. Now, we’re getting more evidence that Dell could indeed launch its Googlebook laptops under the XPS brand. Leaker Evan Blass has shared an image of a Dell product carbon footprint disclosure document in a post on X . We were able to find the document on Dell’s website . The document clearly names the product as the “XPS Googlebook DX13267.” That model number matches the one spotted in the Geekbench listing. Blass adds that the laptop is internally codenamed “Mica.”

title: There’s a serious security fix hiding in Google’s September Pixel update
summary: Google has acknowledged that hackers may have already exploited this Pixel security vulnerability.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s September Pixel security update patches a cellular modem vulnerability that may have been used in limited, targeted attacks. CVE-2026-58704 could allow a remote attacker to bypass permission checks and escalate privileges without requiring any interaction from the victim. CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. Google just released the September Pixel Drop , alongside details of its monthly security fixes for Pixel devices. But amid all the new features that stable Android 17 QPR1 brings, one security flaw may have gone unnoticed. Google and other relevant authorities have now confirmed that a Pixel modem vulnerability, which has now been patched, was used in targeted exploitation.

title: Google doubles down on today’s preview builds with Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5
summary: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 offers Google's latest look at the platform's next big update.
body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 is ready to install on the Pixel 6a and newer hardware. There’s one build for older devices, and another for everything Pixel 8 and newer. In addition to numerous fixes, we’re also spotting changes to the UI and new features. Testing the latest Android preview builds can be a lot of fun for dedicated Pixel users of the right mindset, and today they’ve got their pick of options. We only just saw Google release Android Canary 2609 a little earlier this afternoon, and now Google’s already following that up with the latest Android 17 QPR2 build. With Android 17 QPR1 now stable and out, Pixel owners are looking to QPR2 for an early preview of the changes to expect from Google’s next big platform update, later this year. title: Older Pixel watches just received a major alarm feature from the Pixel Watch 5
summary: Google is expanding its intelligent Smart Wake alarm feature to previous smartwatch generations to end groggy mornings.
body: Credit: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority TL;DR Google is rolling out the Smart Wake alarm feature to the Pixel Watch 2, 3, and 4 as part of the September 2026 Wear OS 7 update. This feature was originally introduced with the Pixel Watch 5. Smart Wake monitors heart rate and subtle movement for a 30-minute window before your set alarm time, then wakes you with gentle haptic vibrations during lighter sleep phases to reduce morning grogginess. Users can access the feature directly inside the Clock app on their Pixel Watch once it has received the new update. One of the standout quality-of-life features Google introduced with the Pixel Watch 5 launch was Smart Wake, giving users a gentler way to start their mornings. Now, Google is bringing that exact experience to older Pixel Watches. As spotted by Reddit user Broad_Magazine2285 , Smart Wake appears to be rolling out more widely to older Pixel Watches, with confirmations that the feature is going live on the Pixel Watch 4, Pixel Watch 3, and Pixel Watch 2. The feature appears to have rolled out as part of yesterday’s September Wear OS 7 update .

The feature isn’t meant to replace your passwords or passkeys but to help recover your Google account. After simplifying third-party sign-ups with your Google account and repeatedly urging you to replace passwords with passkeys, Google now wants you to sign in with a selfie video . Google launched the new sign-in method in July, and while it’s still not available in all regions, it can now be seen prompting users to set up login via selfie video. Google has now started soliciting users to try the video selfie sign-in feature via its homepage on desktop. According to Search Engine Watch , the tech giant has started displaying a banner on its homepage to promote the new sign-in method.

title: Meta’s next smart glasses might not attract perverts, or anyone else
summary: Two steps forward, two steps back.
body: TL;DR Meta might be planning to launch a pair of camera-free smart glasses. They could have six microphones for talking to Meta AI and Muse. The smart glasses could be announced at the Meta Connect conference next week. Meta’s smart glasses seem to be everywhere these days, with their cameras and easily modded LEDs making every moment recordable. With glasses like that, in a design that’s nearly indistinguishable from regular sunglasses, the privacy problems practically write themselves. Well, Meta now seems to be considering a new direction for those who don’t want to be seen as creeps out on the street. According to a new report from The Information , Meta is considering launching smart glasses that skip the camera and focus instead on audio and AI features. Internally codenamed “Luna,” the glasses will reportedly feature six microphones, letting users chat with Meta AI and the company’s agentic AI, Muse . They could also include a side button to quickly launch Meta AI and could carry forward the same speaker setup we’ve seen on Meta’s existing smart glasses.

title: 5 Android phones you should buy instead of the iPhone 18 Pro
summary: Maybe leave that Apple in the cart.
body: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro series a few days ago, and as is often the case with a new iPhone, this year’s changes feel more evolutionary than revolutionary. That’s not necessarily a bad thing. The iPhone 18 Pro still looks incredibly premium, especially in the new Burgundy finish, and the variable-aperture camera is easily one of its more interesting upgrades. But as good as the iPhone 18 Pro looks, it isn’t the only flagship worth spending your money on. Android phones have become incredibly good over the past few years, and depending on what you actually want from your next phone, some alternatives arguably offer even more.

title: I almost missed the Pixel 11’s best camera feature because Google hid it in the settings
summary: Don't spend another minute without the new Quick Access controls.
body: Google’s entire philosophy around the Pixel lineup has been one of simplicity, and that extends to how the Pixel’s camera operates. The idea has always been to create a point-and-shoot experience where you point the phone at something, press the shutter button, and let Google’s software handle the rest. That approach largely works well, but it can also leave you wanting more control when you actually care about how a photo looks. More so, today, when people are looking for a bit more individuality and flavor in photographs. I’m aware of the Pixel camera’s built-in Pro mode, which gives you granular control over shots, but most days I’m not looking to scroll through a long list of manual controls. A few essentials that help me tweak my image without having to get into full manual control territory are what I need.

title: The big Googlebook moment is almost here, and I couldn’t care less
summary: Googlebook has a lot to prove — and Gemini isn't enough.
body: Google’s laptop endeavors are finally getting their long-overdue love. The company is sprucing up the iconic Chromebook ideology into something called Googlebook , which brings together the best of Android and Chrome OS. It carries forward both the good and the bad of its past self, but this time, everything is built around Gemini to give you an AI-first experience. All those big words sound like Google is finally doing something substantial with its laptop efforts. However, the reality is that I couldn’t care less about the Googlebook. Considering the direction Google is putting all its efforts in and how the laptop market is shaping up, I sure wouldn’t bet big on Google’s renewed enthusiasm towards its laptop OS.

title: Android Auto just got a much brighter future in GM vehicles
summary: A clever split-screen setup keeps your phone and truck features together.
body: TL;DR GM’s new infotainment system for the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra keeps Android Auto around despite the company’s earlier plans to move away from it. Android Auto can now run alongside native GM features such as vehicle status and trailering information in a new split-screen layout. The interface will eventually expand across GM’s gas, diesel, and electric vehicles, suggesting Android Auto still has a place in the company’s future. GM’s breakup with Android Auto has been anything but clean. The company first dropped phone projection from newer EVs, then said the same strategy would eventually reach its gas-powered lineup . GM later softened that stance, saying Android Auto and CarPlay would remain available in gas-powered vehicles for the “foreseeable future.” Its latest trucks now suggest that the future could be longer — and more interesting — than expected. The company has unveiled a new infotainment interface for the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra, and Android Auto isn’t merely surviving the redesign. It’s becoming more tightly integrated with GM’s own software.

title: This cheap handheld can emulate games, but also plays your physical GBA cartridges
summary: It won't break the bank, either.
body: Credit: GAMEMT TL;DR The GAMEMT MTX is a new sub-$100 handheld that has a cartridge slot for Game Boy Advance games. It can also emulate SNES, Genesis, PS1, and PSP games via conventional ROM files. The MTX is available at a promotional price of $80 via the official website. The Analogue Pocket still stands out today thanks to its integrated cartridge slot, allowing you to play your physical games on a more modern handheld. Unfortunately, it doesn’t emulate digital game ROMs. But what if you don’t want to choose between a conventional emulation experience and physical cartridges? That’s where the GAMEMT MTX comes in, from the same company that brought you the Pocket Super Knob 5000 . GAMEMT has recently released the MTX (h/t: Retro Handhelds ). This is an emulation-focused handheld that also comes with a Game Boy Advance cartridge slot. This means you can play physical GBA cartridges via emulation, or switch to emulating other consoles via ROM files.
